issues.description: SealSaloon.checkOrderReady is specified as a public no-argument method (UML shows +checkOrderReady(): void), but the solution implements it as checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) and orderMeal calls it with an argument. Students following the specification will implement checkOrderReady() and will not match the reference API/signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the public API to match the spec by implementing `public void checkOrderReady()` with no parameters. If logging is needed, keep it as a private helper (e.g., `private void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)`) and have the no-arg method delegate to it.

issues.description: The problem statement is internally inconsistent about SealSaloon.stock: the UML association lists it as an instance field (SealSaloon -> Stock : stock), while the text explicitly requires `stock` (and methods using it) to be static/shared across all SealSaloon instances. This ambiguity can mislead students on whether to implement an instance field/getter or a static field/getter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent by updating the UML/wording to clearly indicate `stock` is static (shared) and accessed via a static getter (or, alternatively, remove the 'static' requirement if an instance field is intended).

issues.description: Stock exposes a public setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[]) method in the template, but this method is not listed in the UML/specification for Stock. This creates a mismatch in the advertised public API and may cause students to rely on a method that is not part of the required design.
issues.suggestedFix: Either document `setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[])` in the UML/spec (as an allowed helper), or reduce its visibility (e.g., package-private) so the public API matches the diagram.
